title: Blood Relations
intro: Blood-relation questions describe family links in words or code and ask how two people are related. The reliable method is to draw a family tree: use symbols for gender (a triangle for male, a circle for female), '=' for a married couple, and vertical lines for parent-child. Read the sentence left to right, place each person, and the answer is read straight off the diagram. Never carry the chain in your head.

items.name: Male / Female
items.formula: triangle for male, circle for female

items.name: Siblings
items.formula: same horizontal level under one parent line

items.name: "of" reading
items.formula: work from the last named person backwards

topics.name: Relation Terms
topics.details: Lock in the vocabulary: paternal vs maternal (father's vs mother's side), in-laws, niece/nephew, first cousins, and the 'grand'/'great-grand' levels. Many SSC items are pure definition checks — 'mother's brother' is your maternal uncle.

unsolved.problem: Father's sister is your?
Brother's son is your?
Mother's mother is your?
Daughter's husband is your?
Wife's brother is your?

topics.name: Single-Person Relations
topics.details: These chain several links: 'A is the son of B, B is the sister of C — how is C related to A?'. Solve from the last person backwards, keeping a gender flag on each person.

solved.problem: A is the son of B. B is the sister of C. How is C related to A?
solved.solution: B is A's mother; C is B's sibling → C is A's maternal uncle or aunt.

solved.problem: P is the father of Q. Q is the mother of R. How is P related to R?
solved.solution: Q is R's mother, P is Q's father → P is R's maternal grandfather.

solved.problem: X is the brother of Y. Y is the father of Z. How is X related to Z?
solved.solution: X and Y are siblings; Y is Z's father → X is Z's paternal uncle.

solved.problem: M is the wife of N. N is the son of O. How is O related to M?
solved.solution: N is M's husband; O is N's parent → O is M's father-in-law or mother-in-law.

unsolved.problem: A is the daughter of B. B is the son of C. How is C related to A?
P is the mother of Q. Q is the brother of R. How is P related to R?
X is the husband of Y. Y is the sister of Z. How is Z related to X?
A is the son of B. C is the mother of B. How is C related to A?
M is the brother of N. N is the father of O. How is M related to O?

topics.name: Family Tree (Pointing)
topics.details: 'Pointing-to-a-photo' items: a person describes a relation through themselves ('She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son'). Resolve the innermost phrase first, then build outward.

solved.problem: Pointing to a man: 'He is the son of my grandfather's only son.' Who is he?
solved.solution: Grandfather's only son = speaker's father; his son = speaker (if male) or speaker's brother.

solved.problem: 'She is the daughter of my mother.' Who is she (speaker is male)?
solved.solution: Daughter of speaker's mother = speaker's sister.

solved.problem: 'He is the brother of my father's wife.' Who is he?
solved.solution: Father's wife = mother; her brother = maternal uncle.

solved.problem: 'She is the wife of my father's only son' (speaker female, has one brother). Who is she?
solved.solution: Father's only son = speaker's brother; his wife = sister-in-law.

unsolved.problem: 'He is the father of my brother.' Who is he?
'She is the mother of my son.' Who is she (speaker male)?
'He is the only brother of my mother.' Who is he?
'She is the daughter of my father's wife.' (speaker male) Who?
'He is the son of my father's father.' Who is he?

topics.name: Coded Relations
topics.details: Symbols stand for relations: e.g., 'A + B' means A is the father of B, 'A - B' means A is the wife of B. Substitute each symbol with its meaning, build the tree, then read off the asked relation.

solved.problem: If A + B means A is father of B, and B × C means B is brother of C, then in 'P + Q × R', how is P related to R?
solved.solution: P is father of Q; Q is brother of R → P is father of R.

solved.problem: If A - B means A is wife of B, then in 'X - Y', how is Y related to X?
solved.solution: X is the wife of Y → Y is the husband.

solved.problem: If A × B means A is brother of B, and A + B means A is mother of B, then in 'M + N × O', how is M related to O?
solved.solution: M is mother of N; N is brother of O → M is mother of O.

solved.problem: If P + Q means P is parent of Q, then in 'P + Q + R', how is P related to R?
solved.solution: P is parent of Q; Q is parent of R → P is grandparent of R.

unsolved.problem: A + B = A father of B; A × B = A sister of B. In 'X + Y × Z', how is X related to Z?
hints: X father of Y; Y sister of Z.

unsolved.problem: A - B = A wife of B. In 'M - N', how is N related to M?
A + B = A mother of B; A - B = A husband of B. In 'P - Q + R', how is P related to R?
hints: P husband of Q; Q mother of R.

unsolved.problem: A + B = A parent of B. In 'A + B + C', how is A related to C?
A × B = A brother of B. In 'X × Y', Y could be X's?

shortcuts: Always draw a tree: triangle male, circle female, = couple, vertical line = parent-child.
Resolve the innermost phrase first ("grandfather's only son" = father).
Solve chains from the LAST named person backwards.
Keep a gender flag on every person — the final relation often needs it.
For coded items, write the key, substitute, then read the tree.
mistakes: Assuming gender that is not given (uncle vs aunt).
Reading "son of" the wrong way round in a chain.
Forgetting in-law links go through marriage, not blood.
Carrying a long chain mentally instead of drawing it.
pyq: SSC asks one chained relation and one coded-relation item per Tier. A clean tree turns both into a one-line read.
summary: Draw the family tree with gender and marriage symbols, resolve inner phrases first, and solve chains backwards from the last person. Decode symbol keys before building. Never assume an unstated gender — that is the single biggest trap in this chapter.
